description: Hover payloads for receptor layers on the body map: (1) receptors that shape human connection and (2) sex-steroid and HPG-axis receptors in brain, gonads and reproductive tracts. Universal-audience labels + exact receptor names. Content source: white-papers/receptors-human-connections.md (map-content source). Panel copy: body-map/overlays/receptors-sex-hormones-panel.md.

schema_notes.sex: 'male' | 'female' | 'both' — which reference body shows the region
schema_notes.atlas_targets: [{project, mesh_or_system_hint}] — where to pin the overlay in an existing atlas. Female mesh names were checked against slorksmo/Human-Atlas app/anatomy.ts (HRA female v1.10). BodyParts3D male mesh names marked 'confirm' must be checked against the viewer's /models/atlas.json.
schema_notes.hotspot: true when the target is smaller than any available mesh (e.g. a brain nucleus, a cell type); render as a pin on the parent mesh
schema_notes.sex_note: optional, evidence-backed sex difference; see sources/receptors-sources.md

prefer: slorksmo/Human-Atlas (male BodyParts3D 4.0 + female HRA v1.10; has a 'brain' regions system)
atlas_binding.license_notes: Keep BodyParts3D and HuBMAP HRA (CC BY 4.0) attribution. Do not redistribute meshes without a licence check.
atlas_binding.rule: Overlays and copy only — no new viewer, no new meshes.

regions.label: Amygdala

hover.title: Social salience gate
hover.summary: Tags faces and situations as safe, special, or scary — receptors here tint the tag.

receptors.role: can soften threat bias in context

hover.title: Story editor
hover.summary: Helps turn raw receptor chatter into choices — approach, comfort, or step back.

hover.summary: OXTR on heart and vessels means bonding chemistry is not brain-only — the body listens too.

receptors.role: peripheral partner to central bonding signals

regions.label: Uterus

hover.title: Classic OXTR tissue
hover.summary: Famous for labor biology — a reminder that ‘connection receptors’ also run life’s practical scripts.

regions.sex_note: Female map only. OXTR density in myometrium rises through pregnancy and peaks in early labor (Fuchs et al. 1982). See uterus.endometrium and uterus.myometrium for the steroid layer.

female edition (HRA female v1.10) · system:brain › nearest segmented midbrain: 'substantia nigra' (VTA sits medial; hotspot)

hover.title: Dopamine launch pad
hover.summary: Sends dopamine to the reward pocket. Oxytocin can nudge it, so social moments feel worth repeating.

receptors.role: links social cues to dopamine release
opioids loosen the brake on dopamine cells

hover.title: Bond glue (in voles)
hover.summary: In prairie voles, vasopressin receptors here help a male prefer one partner. Human mapping is still indirect.

hover.title: Social-pain alarm
hover.summary: Being left out lights these up. µ-opioid tone helps set how much rejection hurts.

receptors.role: buffers the sting of social pain

regions.label: Lateral septum

atlas_targets.mesh_or_system_hint: system:nervous › brain (no nucleus-level mesh in BodyParts3D; place a hotspot)

hover.summary: Helps tell familiar from new. Vasopressin and oxytocin receptors here show sex differences in rodents.

regions.sex_note: Rodent vasopressin fibres and receptor binding in the septum differ by sex (reviewed in Dumais & Veenema 2016).

regions.label: Medial preoptic area

atlas_targets.mesh_or_system_hint: system:nervous › brain (no nucleus-level mesh in BodyParts3D; place a hotspot)
female edition (HRA female v1.10) · system:brain › 'hypothalamus' (anterior edge; hotspot)

hover.title: Care & mating switchboard
hover.summary: Steroid and oxytocin receptors meet here. In rats, mothers who lick their pups more carry more estrogen-boosted OXTR here.

receptors.role: turns up OXTR and care circuits

regions.sex_note: Estrogen-inducible OXTR binding here tracks maternal care in female rats (Champagne et al. 2001).

regions.label: Hypothalamus · kisspeptin → GnRH neurons

atlas_targets.mesh_or_system_hint: system:nervous › brain (no nucleus-level mesh in BodyParts3D; place a hotspot)
female edition (HRA female v1.10) · system:brain › 'hypothalamus'
male edition (BodyParts3D 4.0) · system:nervous › brain (hotspot)

hover.title: Puberty ignition
hover.summary: Kisspeptin knocks on KISS1R on GnRH cells. They fire in pulses. No working KISS1R, no puberty.

regions.sex_note: Same receptors in both sexes. Females add a mid-cycle positive-feedback surge; males keep steadier pulses.

atlas_targets.mesh_or_system_hint: system:endocrine › 'pituitary gland' (BodyParts3D name; confirm in atlas.json)
male edition (BodyParts3D 4.0) · system:endocrine › pituitary gland

hover.title: LH & FSH factory
hover.summary: GnRH pulses hit GNRHR. Gonadotrope cells answer with LH and FSH. Constant GnRH shuts them down.

receptors.role: (corticotropes) stress axis — same gland, other cells

atlas_targets.mesh_or_system_hint: system:reproductive › 'testis' (interstitial cells are not meshed; hotspot)
male edition (BodyParts3D 4.0) · system:reproductive › testis

hover.title: Testosterone kitchen
hover.summary: LH docks on LHCGR. cAMP rises. Cholesterol moves into mitochondria and becomes testosterone.

atlas_targets.mesh_or_system_hint: system:reproductive › 'testis' (seminiferous tubules; hotspot)
male edition (BodyParts3D 4.0) · system:reproductive › testis

hover.title: Sperm nursery staff
hover.summary: Sertoli cells carry FSHR and AR. Testosterone acts through their AR — not the sperm's — to finish meiosis.

receptors.role: needed for meiosis to finish (mouse SCARKO)

atlas_targets.mesh_or_system_hint: system:reproductive › 'epididymis' (confirm name)
male edition (BodyParts3D 4.0) · system:reproductive › epididymis

hover.title: Sperm finishing school
hover.summary: A 'female' hormone at work in males: ERα in the efferent ducts soaks up fluid so sperm leave concentrated.

atlas_targets.mesh_or_system_hint: system:reproductive › 'prostate'
male edition (BodyParts3D 4.0) · system:reproductive › prostate

hover.title: Androgen-loving gland
hover.summary: Converts testosterone to stronger DHT and listens hard through AR. ERβ was first cloned from this gland (rat).

atlas_targets.mesh_or_system_hint: system:reproductive › 'seminal vesicle' (confirm name)
male edition (BodyParts3D 4.0) · system:reproductive › seminal vesicle

hover.title: Fluid factory
hover.summary: Makes most of the semen fluid. Size and output depend on androgen signalling through AR.

regions.label: Penis · erectile tissue

atlas_targets.mesh_or_system_hint: system:reproductive › 'corpus cavernosum of penis' (confirm name)
male edition (BodyParts3D 4.0) · system:reproductive › penis

hover.title: Blood-flow switch
hover.summary: Nerves release NO. Its receptor, soluble guanylyl cyclase, makes cGMP and relaxes smooth muscle. α1-adrenoceptors keep it soft at rest.

receptors.plain: Soluble guanylyl cyclase — the NO receptor

regions.sex_note: Receptor-exact only: PDE5 is an enzyme that breaks cGMP, not a receptor (Andersson 2011).

atlas_targets.mesh_or_system_hint: female edition (HRA female v1.10) · system:reproductive › 'ovary' (follicles not meshed; hotspot)

hover.title: Estrogen finishers
hover.summary: FSH via FSHR switches on aromatase. They turn the theca's androgens into estradiol. Late in the cycle they gain LHCGR too.

receptors.role: induced by LH surge; needed for ovulation (PR-A, mouse)

atlas_targets.mesh_or_system_hint: female edition (HRA female v1.10) · system:reproductive › 'ovary' (hotspot)

hover.title: Androgen makers in the ovary
hover.summary: LH via LHCGR makes theca cells produce androgens — the raw material for estrogen. Yes, ovaries make androgens.

atlas_targets.mesh_or_system_hint: female edition (HRA female v1.10) · system:reproductive › 'ovary' (hotspot)

hover.title: Progesterone pop-up gland
hover.summary: After ovulation the follicle becomes a temporary gland. LH — or hCG in early pregnancy — keeps it making progesterone.

receptors.role: keeps progesterone flowing; hCG rescue in pregnancy

atlas_targets.mesh_or_system_hint: female edition (HRA female v1.10) · system:reproductive › 'fallopian tube'

hover.title: Egg's escalator
hover.summary: Steroid receptors tune the beating hairs and muscle that move the egg toward the uterus.

atlas_targets.mesh_or_system_hint: female edition (HRA female v1.10) · system:reproductive › 'uterus' (inner layer; hotspot)

hover.title: Monthly rebuild
hover.summary: Estrogen via ERα grows the lining. Progesterone via PR makes it ready to host an embryo.

receptors.role: implantation readiness; PR-A essential in mouse

atlas_targets.mesh_or_system_hint: female edition (HRA female v1.10) · system:reproductive › 'uterus' (muscle wall; hotspot)

hover.title: Labor engine
hover.summary: OXTR numbers climb through pregnancy and peak in early labor. Progesterone keeps the muscle calm until then.

atlas_targets.mesh_or_system_hint: female edition (HRA female v1.10) · system:reproductive › 'cervix'

hover.title: The gatekeeper
hover.summary: Estrogen and progesterone flip its mucus between 'come in' (thin) and 'stay out' (thick).

atlas_targets.mesh_or_system_hint: female edition (HRA female v1.10) · system:reproductive › 'vagina'

hover.title: Estrogen-fed lining
hover.summary: ERα keeps the lining thick and moist. Low estrogen after menopause thins it.

regions.label: Breast · mammary gland

atlas_targets.mesh_or_system_hint: female edition (HRA female v1.10) · system:integumentary/reproductive › 'mammary gland', 'mammary lobes', 'main lactiferous ducts', 'nipple'

hover.title: Grow, branch, deliver
hover.summary: ERα grows the ducts. PR-B branches them in pregnancy. OXTR squeezes milk out when a baby suckles.

regions.sex_note: Males have breast tissue with the same receptors; it stays small unless the estrogen/androgen balance shifts.
